title: Second point: own-justification certainty is not held as firm as faith that Christ is God's Son
source_text: CXXXIII. Nec minus evidenter probare possum non omnes Scholae Reformatae Doctores sentire & docere, quod singuli fideles tam firmiter & certo persuasi esse debeant se esse justos coram Deo, & sibi esse remissa peccata, adeoque salutis aeternae se fore compotes; quam certo credere tenentur Christum esse Dei filium, & mundi Redemptorem, & similia fidei Christianae dogmata: ac per consequens falsum & calumniosum esse, si quis dicat a Reformatis istud communi consensu doceri. Et primo quidem ex eo quod plurimi ex Reformatis, sicut jam ostensum est, agnoscunt talem persuasionem de propria salute, & remissione peccatorum suorum, posse saltem ad longum tempus, a fide separari, & non esse fidei salvificae essentialem, sed ad perfectionem ejus accidentalem solummodo pertinere, ex eo, inquam, manifeste sequitur, juxta eorum sententiam, id fidelibus tam firmiter persuasum esse non debere, quam hoc quod Jesus Christus sit Dei filius, & mundi Redemptor. Nam certa persuasio de hoc articulo non potest a vera fide separari: neque potest aliquis ea persuasione ad tempus destitui, & tamen vere fidelis manere, secundum receptam & omnibus probatam Scholae Reformatae doctrinam.
pass_a_gloss: Nor can I less evidently prove that not all Doctors of the Reformed School think and teach that each of the faithful ought to be so firmly and certainly persuaded that they are just before God, and that their sins are remitted to them, and thus that they will be partakers of eternal salvation, as they are bound certainly to believe that Christ is the Son of God, and the Redeemer of the world, and similar dogmas of the Christian faith: and consequently that it is false and calumnious if anyone says that this is taught by the Reformed by common consent. And first indeed from this — that very many of the Reformed, as has already been shown, acknowledge that such persuasion concerning their own salvation and the remission of their sins can at least for a long time be separated from faith, and is not essential to saving faith, but pertains only to its accidental perfection — from this, I say, it manifestly follows, according to their judgment, that that ought not to be so firmly persuaded to the faithful as this, that Jesus Christ is the Son of God and Redeemer of the world. For certain persuasion concerning this article cannot be separated from true faith: nor can anyone be for a time destitute of that persuasion and yet remain truly faithful, according to the received and universally approved doctrine of the Reformed School.
pass_b_english: Not all Reformed doctors teach that each believer must be as firmly sure of personal justification and eternal salvation as of the dogma that Christ is God's Son and the world's Redeemer — so calling that common consent is false calumny.

Many Reformed already grant that own-salvation persuasion can be separated from faith for a long time and belongs only to faith's accidental perfection — so it cannot bind with the same firmness as the Christ-article, which no one can lose even briefly and still remain truly faithful.

lemmas.gloss: that Christ is the Son of God
